details: Bitcoin rose above $82,000, reaching $82,205, recovering from a recent dip to $79,770. This upward movement is attributed to a weakening US dollar, improved risk sentiment across financial markets, and reduced expectations for a near-term Federal Reserve interest rate hike. Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded net inflows of $5.1 million, with BlackRock's ETF attracting significant capital. Ether also saw a recovery, increasing by 0.3% to $2,457.
title: Bitcoin Rebounds Above $82K Amid Dollar Weakness & Tech Recovery

details: Digital asset investment products globally experienced $434 million in outflows this week. This downturn in sentiment follows the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, which suggests a less supportive macroeconomic environment for digital assets. The outflows highlight Bitcoin's sensitivity to monetary policy, as higher interest rate expectations and tighter financial conditions reduce liquidity for risk-on assets.
title: Global Crypto Funds See $434M Outflows Post-CPI Data

details: Deutsche Bank is set to introduce cryptocurrency custody services, with Bitcoin and Ethereum being the first assets supported. The service launch is expected within weeks in Germany, with plans to expand into Asian financial centers by 2027. This initiative is part of the bank's broader strategy, which includes stablecoin transactions, tokenized deposits, and blockchain-based securities.
title: Deutsche Bank Prepares to Launch Bitcoin & Ethereum Custody

details: Coinbase has expanded its partnership with Marqeta, enabling businesses to offer customers payment cards directly funded by their stablecoin holdings. Marqeta will manage card issuance and processing, while Coinbase will secure the digital assets and handle their conversion to traditional currencies. Settlements for these transactions will utilize the Base network.
title: Coinbase & Marqeta Partner for Stablecoin-Funded Payment Cards

details: Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire announced plans to expand its USD Coin (USDC) stablecoin into approximately 40 new emerging and developing markets. Allaire highlighted increasing demand for digital dollars in regions across Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East. He also noted the potential for AI software to drive small payments using USDC.
title: Circle Eyes 40 New Markets for USDC Expansion
